name: AI Deep Dive — LBRT — 2026-05-02
rationale: Liberty Oilfield Services is a hydraulic fracturing company in deep fundamental deterioration. Revenue peaked at $4.75B in FY2022 (Russia/Ukraine energy crisis cycle) and has declined every year since. Net margins have collapsed from 11.7% to 3.7% TTM. EPS peaked at $3.24 and has declined to $0.91. Forward EPS consensus is $0.31 (Y1) and $0.35 (Y2) — 66% below TTM. Piotroski 3/9. Weighted DCF fair value $12.60 vs $32.68 current = SELL (-61.4%). The forward PE of 92x on near-zero earnings is the clearest SELL signal.

bear.rationale: Oil price weakness drives further E&P capex cuts. Frac activity declines. Revenue falls 5% CAGR ($3.1B by Y5). Margin near breakeven (1%) as pricing power erodes and fixed costs weigh on falling revenue. LBRT competes with ProPetro (PUMP), NexTier, and C&J Energy in a commoditized market. No durable pricing advantage. Exit PE 8x on near-zero EPS = $0.72 PV. Historical precedent: oilfield services companies traded below book value during 2015-2016 and 2020 oil busts.

base.rationale: Analyst-anchored: Y1 $4.31B (+7.6%), Y2 $4.59B (+6.5%). 5-yr CAGR 4% within ±3pp of blended 7%. Net margin 4% = slight improvement from 3.7% TTM as volume growth provides some operating leverage. Exit PE 14x = oilfield services median (cyclical discount; Energy Equipment & Services median 12-18x). QM 0.90: LBRT has Liberty Direct Wireline integration providing some service bundling advantage, but no pricing power in excess of commodity cycle. Year 5: $4,874M × 4% / 159M shares = $1.26 EPS × 14 × 0.90 / 1.6105 = $9.83.

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Oil price recovery to $90+ driven by geopolitical supply disruption + natural gas demand surge for LNG/data center power. E&P capex accelerates. LBRT's completion services in the Permian and DJ basins see strong volume recovery. Margin recovers to 8% (FY2022 peak was 11.7%). Exit PE 20x. Bull fair value $39.64 — only slightly above current $32.68, illustrating the poor risk/reward even in the bull case.

aiThesis.rationale: Liberty Oilfield Services is a hydraulic fracturing company caught in a post-energy-crisis deceleration cycle. The company rode the Russia/Ukraine energy premium to record revenues ($4.75B in FY2022) and margins (11.7%), but every subsequent year has seen revenue and margin decline. Today, TTM revenue is $4.0B (declining), TTM margin is 3.7% (declining), and the forward PE is 92x on analyst EPS of $0.31 — the market is paying 92 years of current earnings for a commodity service company. The three DCF scenarios all produce fair values well below the current price: bear $0.72, base $9.83, bull $39.64. Notably, even the bull case — which requires oil price recovery to $90+ and margin restoration to FY2022 peak levels — only produces $39.64, barely above today's $32.68. This is a classic commodity cyclical trading at the wrong point in the cycle: investors are paying cycle-peak P/E multiples for trough earnings, without the conviction that a cycle recovery is imminent. SELL.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: API shares_diluted = shares_outstanding = 163,191,416. Mktcap-implied: $5.33B / $32.68 = 163.1M — 0.1% discrepancy. Clean.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: Declining trend (not mean-reverting). Historical: 9.6% → 11.7% → 7.3% → 3.7% (TTM). Declining every year from FY2022 peak. Analyst Y1 EPS $0.31 / $4.31B revenue = 1.2% forward GAAP margin — further compression. Using declining-trend framework: base 4% (modest recovery from 3.7% TTM toward mid-cycle), bear 1% (near breakeven), bull 8% (FY2022 cycle peak restoration).
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 $4.31B (+7.6%), Y2 $4.59B (+6.5%). Blended ~7%. Base 4% CAGR reflects expected growth tapering after Y2 (E&P spending cycles moderate). Bull 8% = oil price recovery. Bear -5% = E&P capex contraction. Note: revenue grew strongly in 2021-2022 (Russia/Ukraine energy crisis) and has been declining since. The 4.5% TTM growth metric is misleading — trailing data shows year-over-year growth but full-year revenue is declining from $4.75B peak.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Energy — Oil & Gas Equipment & Services: conservative P/E 8, median P/E 12-18, growth P/E 20-25. Oilfield services are highly cyclical. During downturns, stocks trade below book value. During peaks, 20-25x is achievable.
dataQualityFlags: Revenue DECLINING from peak: $4.15B → $4.75B → $4.32B → $4.01B TTM. The 4.5% TTM revenue growth rate is misleading — comparing to recent quarter, but full-year trend is DOWN from $4.75B peak.
Margin collapse: 9.6% → 11.7% → 7.3% → 3.7% — every year lower. Not mean-reverting. Analyst Y1 $0.31 EPS / $4.31B = 1.2% forward margin — further compression.
Forward PE 92.4x — this is the clearest sell signal. Paying 92x earnings for a commoditized oilfield services company in margin compression is not justified.
Piotroski 3/9: ROA positive and CFO positive are the only positives. ROA not improving, leverage increasing, current ratio declining. Deteriorating financial health.
Analyst target $32.77 ≈ current $32.68 — essentially no upside priced by analysts. Buy rating with 0% target upside is a contradiction.

priorAnalysisReview.assumptionAudit: Prior Gemini SELL at $18.75 — directionally correct. Gemini base: 5% growth, 4% margin, 15x PE, QM 1.0. My base: 4% growth, 4% margin, 14x PE, QM 0.90 — very similar. Our FV $12.60 is lower than Gemini's $18.75 mainly due to lower QM (0.90 vs 1.0) and lower exit PE (14 vs 15). Both analyses agree: significant overvaluation at current price.

Completion activity in Permian remains steady but pricing for frac services under pressure as multiple service companies compete for contracts.
